scene.label: Act 1, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. Another room in Leonato's house.

lines.text: What the good-year, my lord! why are you thus out of measure sad?
lines.plainText: What the goodyear my lord why are you thus out of measure sad

lines.text: There is no measure in the occasion that breeds; therefore the sadness is without limit.
lines.plainText: There is no measure in the occasion that breeds therefore the sadness is without limit

lines.text: You should hear reason.
lines.plainText: You should hear reason

lines.text: And when I have heard it, what blessings brings it?
lines.plainText: And when I have heard it what blessings brings it

lines.text: If not a present remedy, at least a patient sufferance.
lines.plainText: If not a present remedy at least a patient sufferance

lines.text: I wonder that thou (being as thou say'st thou art, born under Saturn) goest about to apply a moral medicine to a mortifying mischief. I cannot hide what I am: I must be sad when I have cause, and smile at no man's jests; eat when I have stomach, and wait for no man's leisure; sleep when I am drowsy, and tend on no man's business; laugh when I am merry, and claw no man in his humour.
lines.plainText: I wonder that thou being as thou say'st thou art born under Saturn goest about to apply a moral medicine to a mortifying mischief I cannot hide what I am I must be sad when I have cause and smile at no man's jests eat when I have stomach and wait for no man's leisure sleep when I am drowsy and tend on no man's business laugh when I am merry and claw no man in his humour

lines.text: Yea; but you must not make the full show of this till you may do it without controlment. You have of late stood out against your brother, and he hath ta'en you newly into his grace; where it is impossible you should take true root but by the fair weather that you make yourself: it is needful that you frame the season for your own harvest.
lines.plainText: Yea but you must not make the full show of this till you may do it without controlment You have of late stood out against your brother and he hath ta'en you newly into his grace where it is impossible you should take true root but by the fair weather that you make yourself it is needful that you frame the season for your own harvest

lines.text: I had rather be a canker in a hedge than a rose in his grace; and it better fits my blood to be disdained of all than to fashion a carriage to rob love from any: in this, though I cannot be said to be a flattering honest man, it must not be denied but I am a plain-dealing villain. I am trusted with a muzzle and enfranchised with a clog; therefore I have decreed not to sing in my cage. If I had my mouth, I would bite; if I had my liberty, I would do my liking: in the meantime, let me be that I am, and seek not to alter me.

lines.text: Can you make no use of your discontent?
lines.plainText: Can you make no use of your discontent

lines.text: I make all use of it, for I use it only. Who comes here?
lines.plainText: I make all use of it for I use it only Who comes here

lines.text: I came yonder from a great supper: the Prince your brother is royally entertained by Leonato; and I can give you intelligence of an intended marriage.
lines.plainText: I came yonder from a great supper the Prince your brother is royally entertained by Leonato and I can give you intelligence of an intended marriage

lines.text: Will it serve for any model to build mischief on? What is he for a fool that betroths himself to unquietness?
lines.plainText: Will it serve for any model to build mischief on What is he for a fool that betroths himself to unquietness

lines.text: Marry, it is your brother's right hand.
lines.plainText: Marry it is your brother's right hand

lines.text: Who? the most exquisite Claudio?
lines.plainText: Who the most exquisite Claudio

lines.text: Even he.
lines.plainText: Even he

lines.text: A proper squire! And who, and who? which way looks he?
lines.plainText: A proper squire And who and who which way looks he

lines.text: Marry, on Hero, the daughter and heir of Leonato.
lines.plainText: Marry on Hero the daughter and heir of Leonato

lines.text: A very forward March-chick! How came you to this?
lines.plainText: A very forward Marchchick How came you to this

lines.text: Being entertained for a perfumer, as I was smoking a musty room, comes me the Prince and Claudio, hand in hand, in sad conference: I whipt me behind the arras, and there heard it agreed upon that the Prince should woo Hero for himself, and having obtained her, give her to Count Claudio.

lines.text: Come, come; let us thither: this may prove food to my displeasure. That young start-up hath all the glory of my overthrow: if I can cross him any way, I bless myself every way. You are both sure, and will assist me?
lines.plainText: Come come let us thither this may prove food to my displeasure That young startup hath all the glory of my overthrow if I can cross him any way I bless myself every way You are both sure and will assist me

lines.text: To the death, my lord.
lines.plainText: To the death my lord

lines.text: Let us to the great supper: their cheer is the greater that I am subdued. Would the cook were of my mind! Shall we go to prove what's to be done?
lines.plainText: Let us to the great supper their cheer is the greater that I am subdued Would the cook were of my mind Shall we go to prove what's to be done

lines.text: We'll wait upon your Lordship.
lines.plainText: We'll wait upon your Lordship
